verdict.reasoning: Patient states, "It's been happening for about three days now," referring to the diarrhea.
Patient states, "It's been happening for about three days now," indicating onset about 3 days ago.
Patient says, "nothing funky in my diet or no travels recently," which supports no recent new foods or travel.
When asked frequency, patient answers "Four to five" times per day.
When asked if stools are like water or loose, patient says, "It probably depends on the time of day, to be honest," which implies variation between more and less watery/loose stools.
Patient states, "I threw up once."
On questioning, patient says, "No blood" and then "No, no" when mucus is explained.
In response to fever, patient says, "Maybe a little bit, but it hasn't been that in particular hasn't been too worrying," indicating a possible low-grade fever.
Patient reports, "A little bit of appetite loss, I guess, versus the normal."
Patient affirms, "Yeah, yeah, yeah" to "you're still able to drink quite a bit?" and clinician notes, "you look like you're not dehydrated."
When asked about medications for diarrhea and abdominal pain, patient replies "Nothing yet" to both.
Patient says, "I. Probably at asthma or. Or, I don't know, I guess I still have it," indicating a history of asthma.

Patient confirms inhaler use: "Yes" to using inhalers, and provides a questionable name ("Lexapro"/"Lexipro"), with clinician saying, "I'll have to check that one. Not sure," so inhaler type is not clearly confirmed.
Clinician asks, "Any other medication that you're using over the counter, Anything at all, regularly?" and patient answers, "No."
On allergies, patient responds, "Nothing. Yeah, nothing," and clinician confirms, "No allergies at all."
Patient notes, "My dad had hypertension" and then clarifies "Has hypertension?" followed by "Hypertension. Yeah."
Patient states, "He died of bowel cancer 10 years ago" and when asked age, answers "62."

The transcript describes acute diarrhea with mild symptoms but does not label it as "acute nonspecific diarrhea" or discuss gastroenteritis vs non-infectious causes or classify it as "currently mild." Those are diagnostic interpretations not stated in the transcript.
While the patient has asthma and uses an inhaler, there is no statement that asthma is "stable" or any explicit asthma management assessment.
Patient reports, "He died of bowel cancer 10 years ago" and that he was 62, which corresponds to colorectal cancer in the father at age 62.

Clinician advises, "you could get something called Di Rolite over the counter. So it helps to replenish the salts" and earlier emphasizes, "You still need to drink plenty of water because you're losing a lot of fluids."
Clinician advises, "a soft diet, so avoid dairy, fish, meat, eggs while you're having the diarrhea" and explains soft diet content.

Clinician: "Once you are able to, you know, keep most of it in, you can start off with some just boiled vegetables and mash. Once you're okay with that for about 48 hours, then you can start having meat." This matches the 48-hour tolerance then gradual reintroduction of meat/eggs/fish.
Clinician notes, "although you can't. Milk is not a good idea. Yogurts are a good idea because they are probiotics. It help to build up the normal gut bacteria back."

Clinician says, "if you're going about six to eight times a day, that means there's a high chance that you are having dehydration and you might need to go into hospital at that point in time. If that happens, do get in touch with us again." This ties action to stool frequency, not to "more than 6 to 8" or generalized dehydration signs as stated in the fact.
Clinician advises, "if you're passing blood. We need a stool sample because that means you might... need treatment with antibiotics."

Clinician states, "if your diarrhea doesn't go away in a week's time ... We need a stool sample" and more generally frames one-week duration as a threshold for further evaluation, supporting reevaluation if it lasts more than a week or worsens.
Clinician says, "All this is all recorded in your app, so you can go back. I'll put that all in detail. So ... you can go back and read the notes."
There is no discussion of an asthma management plan, nor instructions to confirm inhaler name, dose, or usage in the future.

While the clinician instructs the patient to review notes in the app, there is no explicit instruction to contact the clinic if symptoms worsen or fail to improve within one week; the one-week threshold is linked to need for stool sample, and contact is tied specifically to high stool frequency/dehydration.

The clinician does not specify return precautions of "fever" or "severe signs of dehydration"; they mention blood in stool, high stool frequency (6–8/day) and possible hospital need but do not enumerate fever or current absence of these signs.

There is no direct follow-up instruction "contact the clinic if symptoms worsen or fail to improve within one week"; follow-up is mentioned only in relation to increased stool frequency or blood in stool, and implicitly for stool sample.
